Sourcing this PKGBUILD for `makepkg --printsrcinfo` is safe. The global/top-level scope contains only variable and array assignments (`pkgname`, `pkgver`, `source`, `sha256sums`, etc.), a couple of bash parameter expansions (`${_name^}` – a bash uppercase builtin, not a command substitution), and function definitions (`package_*`). None of it invokes external commands, downloads anything, or exfiltrates data. 

The `install` commands live inside the `package_otf-garamontio()`, `package_ttf-garamontio()`, and `package_ttf-garamontio-variable()` functions, which are NOT executed during `--printsrcinfo` (only during the packaging phase, and their behavior is ordinary font-file installation into `$pkgdir`). There is no `eval`, no base64/hex-obfuscated payload, no curl/wget of executable content, and no top-level command substitution. The source URLs point to the project's own upstream on codeberg.org. Nothing in the top-level scope can execute attacker-controlled code or exfiltrate data when run with `makepkg --printsrcinfo`.
</details>
<evidence>
